stories.headline: NIS 2 Directive: draft implementing regulation open for feedback
stories.deck: Common incident reporting templates under the NIS2 Directive: a draft by the Commission services, not adopted; feedback until 22 Dec 2026. The NIS2 Directive sets out obligations on essential and important entities in 18 critical sectors in the EU for the reporting of significant cybersecurity incidents. stories.headline_de: EU-Weltraumgesetz: Bericht für das Plenum eingereicht
stories.deck_de: Report of Parliament's Industry, Research and Energy committee on the EU Space Act proposal, adopted in committee on 19 November 2026 and tabled for plenary on 20 November 2026; it is the committee's text for the plenary vote, not Parliament's position and not law.

brief.en: Like the rapporteur's draft report, it removes the proposal's own cybersecurity regime for space operators (risk management, incident reporting and the resilience annex) and instead extends the space sector of the NIS 2 Directive to all space activities, space services and Union-owned assets, with transposition 24 months after entry into force; unlike the draft, it keeps the link to NIS 2 as a without-prejudice clause and drops the reduced duty to report incidents. It also cuts the authorisation deadline to six months with tacit approval where national law allows (not for launch services), adds a security and defence filter for authorisations, exempts SMEs and research institutions from the environmental footprint rules and deletes the Union Space Label; none of the tracked concepts is touched.

It also cuts the authorisation deadline to six months with tacit approval where national law allows (not for launch services), adds a security and defence filter for authorisations, exempts SMEs and research institutions from the environmental footprint rules and deletes the Union Space Label; none of the tracked concepts is touched.

stories.headline: Cloud and AI Development Act: CJ18 draft report
stories.deck: Joint draft report of 17 November 2026 of the co-rapporteurs of the Industry, Research and Energy and the Internal Market committees on the proposed Cloud and AI Development Act, with 366 amendments to the Commission proposal; it is the rapporteurs' draft, not the position of the committees or of Parliament, and not law.
stories.headline_de: CADA: Berichtsentwurf im Parlament
stories.deck_de: Joint draft report of 17 November 2026 of the co-rapporteurs of the Industry, Research and Energy and the Internal Market committees on the proposed Cloud and AI Development Act, with 366 amendments to the Commission proposal; it is the rapporteurs' draft, not the position of the committees or of Parliament, and not law.

brief.en: On data centres it would make the designation of acceleration zones optional and add an impact analysis, grid, water and local benefit requirements, anti-speculation rules for grid reservations and a time-limited priority for Union operators not controlled from third countries. On the cloud sovereignty framework it would add a list of public sector activities assigned to each assurance level (new Annex IIa), a Commission methodology with powers to warn, suspend and take over national recognition, auditors approved by national authorities and limits on delegated acts amending the criteria, while easing some criteria, such as processing of telemetry and operational metadata outside the Union for cybersecurity purposes at levels 1 to 3. It would oblige private entities in the sectors of Annex I to the NIS-2 Directive to assess their cloud workloads and, after a transition, to use recognised services for critical ones, and it raises the procurement target for innovative SMEs from 25 % to 35 %.
brief.de: On data centres it would make the designation of acceleration zones optional and add an impact analysis, grid, water and local benefit requirements, anti-speculation rules for grid reservations and a time-limited priority for Union operators not controlled from third countries. On the cloud sovereignty framework it would add a list of public sector activities assigned to each assurance level (new Annex IIa), a Commission methodology with powers to warn, suspend and take over national recognition, auditors approved by national authorities and limits on delegated acts amending the criteria, while easing some criteria, such as processing of telemetry and operational metadata outside the Union for cybersecurity purposes at levels 1 to 3. It would oblige private entities in the sectors of Annex I to the NIS-2 Directive to assess their cloud workloads and, after a transition, to use recognised services for critical ones, and it raises the procurement target for innovative SMEs from 25 % to 35 %.

stories.headline: Where ENISA consults: ten channels, two feeds, and drafts that are announced elsewhere
stories.deck: ENISA does not publish more than it did in 2023, but in more places and by more rules. Its certification work consults in an orderly way on its own website. Its guidance for manufacturers under the Cyber Resilience Act was put out for comment in 2026 as PDF files on its server, mostly without a news item on its site, and became known through LinkedIn and community mailing lists. The Cybersecurity Act 2 would make such guidance a standing task of ENISA, so far without a duty to consult on it.
stories.headline_de: Wo ENISA konsultiert: zehn Kanäle, zwei Feeds und Entwürfe, die anderswo angekündigt werden
stories.deck_de: ENISA veröffentlicht nicht mehr als 2023, aber an mehr Orten und nach mehr Regeln. Ihre Zertifizierung konsultiert geordnet auf einer eigenen Website. Ihre Leitfäden für Hersteller nach dem Cyber Resilience Act gingen 2026 als PDF-Dateien auf ihrem Server in die Konsultation, meist ohne Meldung auf ihrer Website, und wurden über LinkedIn und Mailinglisten der Community bekannt. Der Cybersecurity Act 2 würde solche Leitfäden zur Daueraufgabe der ENISA machen, bisher ohne Pflicht, dazu zu konsultieren.

stories.headline_de: CADA: neuer Schritt im Verfahren
stories.deck_de: Progress report of the Irish Presidency of 13 November 2026 on the proposed Cloud and AI Development Act, for Coreper to take note of and to pass to the Telecommunications Council of 1 December 2026; it is not a Council position and contains no legal text.

brief.en: It reports a first, partial Presidency compromise text on the autonomy part (the cloud sovereignty framework, public procurement and the public sector cloud federation), discussed in the working party on 10 November 2026: among other things, the Commission's implementing acts on Member States' assurance levels give way to recommendations, the mandated migration period goes from 12 to 18 months, the annual review of audit opinions becomes biennial, and the procurement rules extend to utilities' contracting entities. For the research and data centre parts, still being drafted, it announces among other things a later date of application (18 instead of 12 months after entry into force) and longer deadlines for data centre acceleration zones; the recognition architecture, penalties for SMEs and alignment with the proposed Cybersecurity Act revision and Public Procurement Act remain open.
brief.de: It reports a first, partial Presidency compromise text on the autonomy part (the cloud sovereignty framework, public procurement and the public sector cloud federation), discussed in the working party on 10 November 2026: among other things, the Commission's implementing acts on Member States' assurance levels give way to recommendations, the mandated migration period goes from 12 to 18 months, the annual review of audit opinions becomes biennial, and the procurement rules extend to utilities' contracting entities. For the research and data centre parts, still being drafted, it announces among other things a later date of application (18 instead of 12 months after entry into force) and longer deadlines for data centre acceleration zones; the recognition architecture, penalties for SMEs and alignment with the proposed Cybersecurity Act revision and Public Procurement Act remain open.

stories.headline_de: EU-Weltraumgesetz: Sitzung einer Ratsarbeitsgruppe
stories.deck_de: Progress report on the EU Space Act of 13 November 2026, sent by the General Secretariat of the Council to Coreper and the Council for the Competitiveness Council of 3-4 December 2026, which are invited to take note of it; it records the work of the Irish Presidency, is not a Council position and changes no text.

brief.en: It reports on the Presidency compromise text of 29 October 2026: "EUSA verification" replaces "EUSA registration" for third-country operators and international organisations, the scope excludes space objects operated by military or defence authorities for their entire lifetime or owned by military authorities, a self-certification without a qualified technical body is offered for spacecraft with governmental ownership or operation, the rules on space-based data now centre on Earth observation data bought by public contracting authorities and Union bodies, and the environmental footprint gives way to a life-cycle assessment with a voluntary Union method. On cybersecurity the Presidency did not modify the provisions; the report says the compromise text deals with the scope of the NIS-2 Directive, third-country operators and derogations through two implementing acts. All Member States keep a scrutiny reservation, and the Working Party continues with a view to reaching the Council's position.
brief.de: It reports on the Presidency compromise text of 29 October 2026: "EUSA verification" replaces "EUSA registration" for third-country operators and international organisations, the scope excludes space objects operated by military or defence authorities for their entire lifetime or owned by military authorities, a self-certification without a qualified technical body is offered for spacecraft with governmental ownership or operation, the rules on space-based data now centre on Earth observation data bought by public contracting authorities and Union bodies, and the environmental footprint gives way to a life-cycle assessment with a voluntary Union method. On cybersecurity the Presidency did not modify the provisions; the report says the compromise text deals with the scope of the NIS-2 Directive, third-country operators and derogations through two implementing acts.
